body.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp array belongs, for every \(n\), to Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class.  Its nonzero treated projection retains nonnegligible late rare-arm increments and therefore fails the negligible-increment requirement in their Gaussian Condition 3(ii).  Define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for \(0<d<d_{\max}\),
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r.
 \end{cases}
\]
Also define
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}}u\,du
\]
for \(a\in(0,1)\).  If a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over Li and Zhao's baseline binary class, then for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\), under each sign of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(1-x(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
Only this converse transfers.  Neither the pair-specific attaining allocation nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem is asserted on Li and Zhao's larger class.
body.proof_tex:
For every \(n,t\), define the two binary assignment probabilities by
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
The joint-family properties proposition proves that both are strictly positive, deterministic functions of every history, and sum to one.  It also proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable.  The sourced baseline-class lemma therefore places every finite array in Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.  This conclusion does not use the all-horizon profile contract.

Let \(a\in(0,1)\) and \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  For the treated scalar projection define
\[
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g_a(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g_a(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
The increments are pairwise orthogonal by iterated conditioning.  The cap is inactive for every \(t>\lfloor an\rfloor\) when \(n\) is sufficiently large.  If \(W_n\) denotes the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error, then
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 g_a(t/n)^2\left\{\frac{t}{\bar q_\star(t/n)}-1\right\}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and Riemann convergence gives
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star(a):=\int_a^1\frac{u g_a(u)^2}{\bar q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), the outcome envelope is at least
\[
 g_a(1)=\min\{L_r(1-a),M\}>0,
\]
the regression envelope is zero, and the smaller binary assignment probability is \(\bar q_\star(1)/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the negligible-maximum ratio recorded in the sourced Condition 3(ii) has lower limit at least
\[
 \frac{g_a(1)^2}{\bar q_\star(1)^2w_\star(a)}>0.
\]
It cannot be \(o(1)\).  This establishes the late-increment obstruction directly; it does not assume a Gaussian limit.

Now fix \(0<d<d_{\max}\) and set \(a=1-x(d)\).  Uniform baseline-class honesty and the just-proved every-\(n\) inclusion imply
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \gamma_n
 =\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}
 \le\alpha.
\]
Apply the finite common-subprobability inequality for this selected pair:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
The same finite calculation gives \(\Delta_n^\star\ge d(x(d))=d\), and the void-product calculation gives
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}.
\]
Taking lower limits proves the displayed converse.  The argument uses baseline honesty only to obtain pair honesty and then uses the exact two-law common component; it invokes neither structured-class honesty nor any positive calibration result.  The attaining allocation knows the selected pair, so it does not transfer to the larger baseline class.
body.justification: Every finite optimized-intensity array is in Li and Zhao's baseline class, so baseline-class uniform honesty directly supplies the pair honesty needed by the exact common-void argument.
body.gap: The transfer must avoid relying on this note's all-horizon profile contract, which can fail at finite capped prefixes, while still verifying the published Gaussian negligible-increment obstruction.
body.consumer: Readers may use the joint optimized lower envelope against baseline-class honesty claims, but may not transfer the pair-specific attaining rule or the structured positive calibration theorem.
